Early this month, OpenAI launched its first GPT-6 model equipped with Astra. Now the GPT-6 series welcomes two new members, namely the GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna models.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are now available

According to the release notes of the ChatGPT desktop application, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna require fewer tokens to run than their counterpart GPT-5.6 version.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are rolling out to Codex and ChatGPT Work, with lower token pricing than their predecessor GPT-5.6. Sol is suited for complex coding and agentic workflows, while Luna is suited for focused, high-volume tasks. The two models are being progressively opened up to Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users. Free and Go users can use Luna on the desktop app. Actual availability depends on the rollout schedule and workspace settings; Enterprise administrators must enable the new models before they can be used. In ChatGPT, the new models are available for Work and Codex, but Chat does not currently offer them.

Note that this time there is no GPT-6 Terra model. OpenAI is expected to have dropped the mid-sized model, keeping only three tiers: Terra (small), Sol (large), and Astra (extra-large).

Below is OpenAI's official announcement:

Although the toughest and most important projects still need the full depth of Astra, real-world work varies in scale, pace, and budget. That is exactly why we are expanding the GPT-6 family with GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. GPT-6 Astra pioneered a new generation of intelligence, and these new models extend those benefits further, pushing the frontier on cost-effectiveness. GPT-6 Sol and Luna use training approaches similar to GPT-6 Astra, bringing Astra's state-of-the-art performance in professional work, accuracy, coding, computer use, and alignment to faster, more economical models.

The company says these two newest models are not only more affordable than Astra (and the GPT-5.6 versions they replace) but also more capable. For example, pricing for the GPT-6 versions of Sol and Luna is 50% lower than the GPT-5.6 versions.
